correctness.rationale: With independent coordinate picks, D=sum 1_{N_i>0} and H=sum 1_{N_i odd}; the parity character identities E(-1)^{N_i}=(1-2/n)^t and E(-1)^{N_i+N_j}=(1-4/n)^t yield exact marginal variances; conditioning N_i=0 gives the cross-covariance np/2[1+(n-1)b-na]. Since 1-2/n is a strict convex mixture of 1 and 1-2/(n-1), strict Jensen for t≥2 proves positivity. Taylor expansions at t/n→c produce the stated positive variance limits and rho(c); at t=Θ(nlogn), a=p²[1+O(t/n²)], b=a[1+O(t/n²)], and covariance~np/2 with variances~np,n/4, so correlation~sqrt(p) and exponent −β/2. Independent enumeration of flip sequences n=3,t=2; n=4,t=3; n=5,t=4; n=7,t=5 reproduces five exact moments.
residual_risks: Numerical large-n tests alone do not prove limits; the binomial expansions and tight variance estimates do.

value.rationale: Exploration diversity and parity displacement are two canonical observables of the same hypercube walk. The exact two-scale normalized dependence law identifies when the walk progressively loses linear correlation with the set of explored axes, a natural statistic for random walks/occupancy; beyond the known numerator it needs fresh variance and uniform asymptotics.
residual_risks: Quantitative mixing cutoff, central limit coupling and nonuniform coordinate walks are not addressed.

limitations: At t=1 both statistics deterministic; theorem restricts n≥3,t≥2.
